newsitem.title: UK: Unionist MP sees UK govt surviving until March.
newsitem.headline: Unionist MP sees UK govt surviving until March.

text.p: An Ulster Unionist member of parliament said on Monday he believed the British government could remain in office for the next 3-1/2 months without much difficulty.
William Ross's party, with nine members in the lower House of Commons, is widely seen as a possible ally of the ruling Conservatives now they have lost their parliamentary majority.
He told Reuters in a telephone interview: "The government will easily survive until March 20 (at the least)."
Ross said the Commons was likely to rise for the Christmas recess at the end of next week and not resume its sittings until January 13.

He said it would then be seen as unacceptable to call a general election until new electoral registers came into force on February 15, and March 20 was therefore the earliest possible date for a poll.
Asked about his party's attitude in future parliamentary votes, Ross said: "Ulster Unionists will always act in the best interests of the United Kingdom and of Ulster in particular."

Ross said the Unionists would listen with particular interest to the debate going on in parliament at present on a bill to facilitate arms decommissioning in Northern Ireland, to see the exact stances taken up by the government and the opposition Labour Party. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
